ads_ratio.reason: DATA_GAP:ads_ratio — 20-F filer: engine per-share figures are per ordinary (Series B) share but the Nasdaq price ($11.03) is per ADS; each ADS represents 100 Series B shares, so per-share figures are scaled x100 to be comparable to the traded price.
ads_ratio.source: PT Telkom Indonesia FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements (Form 6-K filed 2025-04-18; Form 20-F for FY2024 filed 2025-04-28), Note 2t: 'Income per ADS is computed by multiplying the basic earnings per share by 100, the number of shares represented by each ADS'; the face of the income statement reads 'Profit per ADS (100 Series B shares per ADS)', and Note 1 records the ratio change effective October 26, 2016 from 1 ADS = 200 Series B shares to 1 ADS = 100 Series B shares. The company's financial highlights state the same: 'Net income per ADS (1 ADS : 100 common stock)'

moat_against: No growth conversion: IDR revenue +1.3% FY2023, +0.5% FY2024, -2.2% FY2025 (company highlights); mobile subscriber base -3.1% YoY at 2Q26 — a saturated, price-competitive market (Indosat, XLSmart)

Governance overhang: SEC and DOJ investigations into revenue recognition, financial reporting and FCPA matters, an ICFR material weakness, restated FY2023/FY2024 figures and a March 2026 non-reliance 6-K (company 6-K disclosures, April 2025 and March 2026)
State control: the government is ultimate parent (FY2024 statements, Note 1) — policy, dividend and management decisions are not purely commercial, and control moved to Danantara in 2025
Currency drag: reporting in IDR with period-end USD translation falling from 6.5e-05 (2022) to 6.2e-05 (2024) in dcf_numbers.json — USD per-share economics shrink even when IDR operations are flat

Capex intensity is structural: FY2024 cash capex Rp26,005B for property and equipment plus Rp3,658B of intangibles (FY2024 cash-flow statement) against OCF of Rp61,600B, before lease principal repayments of Rp7,387B that sit in financing
moat_for: Market leadership at scale: Telkomsel is Indonesia's largest mobile operator (153.5M subscribers at 2Q26, Bina Artha company update) and IndiHome leads fixed broadband (~9.5-10.3M B2C subscribers) — convergence bundling across both raises switching friction

Irreplicable physical base: nationwide fibre backbone, 301,000 BTS on air at 2Q26 (Bina Artha) and licensed spectrum; the FY2024 statements put telecommunication infrastructure at Rp161,035B, 54% of total assets (auditor key audit matter)
Returns well above the cost of capital through the cycle: roic_proxy 18.6-22.8% over FY2020-FY2024 (fundamentals.json) and ~50% EBITDA margin in FY2024 (company highlights)
State anchor shareholder (Danantara 54.5%) and universal-service licences granted for unlimited periods (FY2024 statements, Note 1) — incumbency is structurally protected
Self-funding dividend payer: cash dividend of Rp17,683B paid for FY2023 (FY2024 statements, Note 29) while net debt stayed modest (engine net debt $1,181M)
moat_justification: Indonesia's dominant integrated carrier: Telkomsel is the largest mobile operator and IndiHome the leading fixed-broadband brand, on a nationwide fibre, tower and spectrum base that rivals cannot replicate, with the state (Danantara, 54.5% per UOB Kay Hian 2Q26 update) as controlling holder. The measured franchise supports a real moat: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json (IDR, as filed) ran 22.3% / 22.8% / 18.8% / 19.8% / 18.6% over FY2020-FY2024 — well above the cost of capital through the cycle — and company-reported EBITDA margin was ~50% in FY2024 (Rp75,029B on revenue of Rp149,967B, Telkom financial highlights). Gross margin is not meaningful for this filer (fundamentals.json carries no COGS split; expenses are presented by nature). Capped at 6 because the moat does not convert into growth or pricing power: IDR revenue grew only +1.3% (FY2023) and +0.5% (FY2024) and fell -2.2% in FY2025, mobile subscribers are shrinking (-3.1% YoY in 2Q26), competition from Indosat/XLSmart caps ARPU, and state control now carries an active governance overhang (SEC and DOJ investigations, an auditor material weakness and a March 2026 non-reliance 6-K). A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years.
name: PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk
one_liner: Dominant Indonesian integrated carrier (Telkomsel mobile + IndiHome broadband), moat 6/10 on ~19-23% ROIC through the cycle — the weighted case clears 15% (weighted IRR 19.11%, weighted IV@15% $14.39 vs $11.03 ADS price, base OE $2.23 per ADS for a 20.24% OE yield), but the band spans bear Tier C to bull Tier A and sized to the bear end it clears 15% only at or below the bear IV@15% of $9.46; confidence low — FY2025 20-F is not yet in EDGAR companyfacts (base stops at FY2024), FY2023/FY2024 were restated, and SEC/DOJ investigations with an ICFR material weakness are open.

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has no filed SBC value to band against (last filed value is null under every SBC tag it reads, in every year), so any value flags out-of-band. The $0 is not an estimate — it is the filer's own reported position: its FY2024 audited statements contain no SBC line, note, plan or amount anywhere, its cash-flow statement has no SBC add-back, its equity statement shows no stock-compensation credit, and its EPS note confirms no potentially dilutive instruments exist.
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024 of the last 3 under the engine's tags because the filer reports no share-based compensation at all in those years: no SBC line, note, plan or expense amount appears anywhere in its own FY2024 audited statements (which carry the FY2023 comparatives), and its EPS note confirms no equity-linked dilutive instruments exist. The filing-sourced equity SBC figure for the gap years is $0 (same treatment as COKE/ARCC in this sweep); charging $0 is the filer's own reported position, not a zero-fill of a missing value.
sbc_override.source: PT Telkom Indonesia FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements (furnished on Form 6-K filed 2025-04-18 and included in the Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed 2025-04-28): the words 'share-based' and 'stock option' appear nowhere in the 138-page statements; the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows are presented on the direct method (cash receipts/payments) with no share-based compensation add-back or line for FY2024 or FY2023, and the Consolidated Statements of Changes in Equity show capital stock (Rp4,953B) and additional paid-in capital (Rp2,711B) unchanged across FY2023-FY2024 with movements only from dividends, non-controlling-interest transactions, restructuring differences, OCI and profit — no stock-compensation credit to APIC in either year

shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted shares missing for 2022, 2023, 2024; only the non-diluted WeightedAverageShares count (99,062,216,600 in each year) is tagged. The filer's own EPS note proves diluted = basic for 2023 and 2024 (no potentially dilutive instruments), and the count has been identical at 99,062,216,600 every year since 2017 in financials_history.csv, so applying the same filed count to 2022 changes nothing. shares_override.source: PT Telkom Indonesia FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements (Form 6-K filed 2025-04-18; Form 20-F for FY2024 filed 2025-04-28), Note 28 Basic Earnings Per Share: basic EPS is computed on a weighted average of 99,062,216,600 shares for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, and 'The Company does not have potentially dilutive financial investments for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023' — so the diluted weighted count equals the basic count the engine found under WeightedAverageShares
